name: Dilip Buildcon Ltd
title: Dilip Buildcon Ltd - 540047 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Dilip Buildcon FY26 consolidated PAT rose to INR1,398 crores on revenue down 20.6% to INR8,984 crores; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 standalone revenue fell about 22% to INR7,005 crores, while standalone EBITDA dropped about 19% to INR734 crores and standalone PAT rose to INR841 crores from INR311 crores. Consolidated EBITDA was INR1,766 crores at a 19.6% margin. Management reframed the company into three verticals (EPC, MDO coal mining, and Assets/InvIT) and targets 75% of profit from long-term assets by FY29. Management guided FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40%, EBITDA margin of 11-12%, and INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders, with net debt-free status targeted by FY28.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Builds assets for the group; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores and completions INR2,812 crores. Management targets INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders in FY27 and 30-40% revenue growth.

segments.name: MDO (coal mining)
segments.commentary: FY26 coal production 28.72 million tonnes (Siarmal 22.35 Mt, Pachhwara 6.37 Mt). Revenue from mining about INR1,600 crores currently, guided to about INR2,500 crores in FY27, about INR3,100 crores in FY28 and about INR4,000 crores in FY29. Target 57 Mt by FY29.

segments.name: Assets / InvIT
segments.commentary: Holds about INR1,600 crores of InvIT units. Next tranche of 11 HAM assets expected to yield about INR1,800 crores of InvIT units for incremental investment of INR169 crores, with transfers through Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40% over FY26, supported by an order book of almost INR28,000 crores.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin target of 11-12%.
Targeting INR10,000-12,000 crores of new order inflow in FY27.
Standalone debt reduction of INR600-800 crores in FY27; interest outgo expected at INR375-400 crores; net debt-free by FY28.
Coal production target of about 57 Mt by FY29; Siarmal about 33-35 Mt in FY27 and 50 Mt by FY29.
Management expects about 75% of profit from long-term assets and 25% from EPC by FY29.

Transmission and solar projects: equity requirement about INR1,600 crores (solar about INR1,200 crores, transmission about INR400 crores); DBL targets 15% of equity with 85% from outside investors; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR in high teens; commissioning about 2 years from start.
capex_capacity: Siarmal coal handling plant capex pending; a revenue-share kicker applies once it reaches COD.
Pottangi mine to be set up over the next 3 years.
Next InvIT tranche: 11 HAM assets, transfers 4 assets in Q1 FY27 and the balance in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
Under-construction projects of about INR1,000 crores plus invested, to be transferred to InvIT.
Gross block about INR3,600 crores and net block about INR800 crores, stated to be debt free.
demand_pricing: Average monthly infrastructure tendering in FY26 was about INR1.4 trillion, below the government's FY26 target, due to state elections, regulatory scrutiny and administrative delays.

Bitumen and HSD (diesel) cost inflation from elevated crude prices; government contracts only partly pass this through via WPI/CPI-linked formulas, so some margin impact is expected, mainly in coal where HSD is a major cost.
Coal MDO pricing is contracted per tonne: about INR500 per tonne at Siarmal and about INR1,100 per tonne at Pachhwara.
Q4 mining margin fell temporarily because about 6 Mt of coal is stuck at Siarmal due to delayed government evacuation and rake unavailability.
Management stated 90% of the last 20 years' revenue came from national government and other states, and only 10% from the Madhya Pradesh state government.

qa_highlights.question: Will MDO revenue and profitability be shared quarterly, and what is the profitability outlook after the coal handling plant capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO revenue and profitability will be shared quarterly. Revenue is projected at about INR2,500 crores in FY27 and INR4,000 crores by FY29, with similar margins to be assumed; no monetisation plan for the subsidiaries is announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected InvIT distribution after the transfers, given lower distributions from Alpha?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said transfer timing changed in FY26 and distributions are envisaged in slide 24; FY26 Shrem and Alpha dividend and interest income was INR64.5 crores, with total distributions close to INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are the equity structure, IRR and commissioning timeline for the transmission and solar projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Investors would put in about 85% of equity during construction with DBL 15%; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR high-teens for both. SPVs are formed, lender in-principle approvals obtained, and commissioning is about 2 years from start.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone receivables rise to INR1,783 crores despite lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores of Jal Jeevan Mission final 10% payments, which depend on hydro testing, are pending; they will be paid partly in Q1 and partly in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does coal margin trend, given FY25 blended margin around 26% vs 23% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed a 24-25% stabilised range is the right base, with improvement as volumes scale and the coal handling plant comes online.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pass-through for the raw material escalation from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts are linked to WPI and CPI, so pass-through is partial; NHBF is lobbying the government for relief.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and what drives the interest cost trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of borrowing is about 9%; standalone interest cost fell 11% in FY26 mainly from working capital loan rates cut about 125 bps, partly offset by lower mobilisation advances.

risks_watch: About 6 Mt of coal stuck at Siarmal due to delayed evacuation and rake availability; margin normalisation depends on government logistics.
Raw material inflation (bitumen, HSD) with only partial pass-through under inflation formulas.
Execution of the transmission and solar equity structure depends on finding investors for 85% of INR1,600 crores equity; no investor named.
Receivables rose to INR1,783 crores; about INR400 crores of JJM payment pending hydro testing.
InvIT valuations depend on final BPC values, land handover and scope changes; InvIT unit values on balance sheet are about INR1,600 crores.
Delivery of the net debt-free goal by FY28 relies on InvIT transfers and mining cash flows.
Competitive intensity and high bidding in certain segments.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the mining, InvIT and debt-reduction plan, with specific numeric targets. More cautious on near-term margins, raw material inflation and the Q4 coal evacuation issue, which it called temporary. Some answers on investor names and InvIT valuation were deliberately left open.
key_quotes: by FY29 we anticipate three fourth of our profits to be coming from long-term assets and only one fourth to be coming from our EPC business
we are prioritizing profitability, cash flow visibility and return ratios over pure top line growth
our agenda is to be a net debt-free balance sheet by FY28
